vulnerability.title: Enable authselect
vulnerability.description: Configure user authentication setup to use the authselect tool. If authselect profile is selected, the rule will enable the profile.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then var_authselect_profile='' authselect current if test "$?" -ne 0; then if { rpm --quiet -q kernel rpm-ostree bootc && ! rpm --quiet -q openshift-kubelet && { [ -f "/run/.containerenv" ] || [ -f "/.containerenv" ]; }; }; then authselect select --force "$var_authselect_profile" else authselect select "$var_authselect_profile" fi if test "$?" -ne 0; then if rpm --quiet --verify pam; then authselect select --force "$var_authselect_profile" else echo "authselect is not used but files from the 'pam' package have been altered, so the authselect configuration won't be forced." >&2 fi fi fi else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: The remediation only runs authselect to apply a predefined authentication profile. This is a standard STIG hardening step for PAM/authentication and does not modify bootloader, kernel, or filesystem structures. While an incorrect profile could lock out users, the risk is typical for PAM changes and can be mitigated with pre‑checks, so it is classified as safe to remediate.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: authentication/authorization affected; potential PAM misconfiguration; possible loss of SSH or console authentication if profile is incorrect

review_feedback: Forcing the 'sssd' authselect profile overwrites PAM configuration. If the SSSD package or service is not installed or not correctly configured, the system may lose local authentication (e.g., SSH login), leading to lockout. The plan does not verify the profile's existence or back up current PAM files, increasing risk of service disruption.

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan will enable authselect by selecting the 'sssd' profile, which satisfies the rule. It would be safer to verify that the 'sssd' profile exists on the system and that SSSD is installed and correctly configured before forcing the selection, and to back up current PAM configuration files as a precaution against accidental lockout.
concerns: If the 'sssd' profile is not appropriate for the system (e.g., SSSD is not installed or not used), forcing it could disrupt authentication and lock out users.
No backup of existing PAM configuration is performed prior to the change.
suggested_improvements: Run `authselect list` and confirm that the 'sssd' profile is available.
Check that the sssd package is installed and operational before applying the profile.
Create a backup of /etc/pam.d and any related authselect generated files before invoking the command.
Consider applying the profile without the --force flag first to see if a normal selection is sufficient.
